lines.text: Men from Judea teach that the brothers cannot be saved unless circumcised, so Paul and Barnabas are appointed to go to Jerusalem.
Passing through Phoenicia and Samaria, Paul and Barnabas bring great joy, and in Jerusalem some believers from the Sadducees say Gentiles must be circumcised.
Peter says God gave the Gentiles the Holy Spirit, just as He did to the Jewish believers, and cleansed their hearts by faith.
James judges that Gentiles turning to God should not be troubled, but should abstain from food polluted by idols, sexual immorality, strangled meat, and blood.
The apostles and elders choose Judas called Barsabbas and Timothy to go to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas, carrying a letter.
